source: Eddin AN et al. Anti-Money Laundering Alert Optimization Using Machine Learning with Graphs (arXiv 2112.07508)

quote: The percentage of suspicious accounts in our dataset is less than 3% of the alerted ones, resulting in over 97% false positives. | we consider recall@20%FPR as our target metric, which translates to a reduction of the false positives by 80% compared to the rule system itself | allows us to alert only 20% of the events while capturing over 90% of the suspicious entities
parameter: prevalence pi (share of alerts that are true positives)
limitations: Retrospective validation on one bank's data; account-day labels inferred from SAR transactions; ML (LightGBM) triage, not gen-AI

quote: auto-closed share = 0.8(1-pi) + (1-recall)pi; miss rate inside closed band = (1-recall)pi / auto-closed share
parameter: h (auto-closed share) and e (error inside auto-closed band)
value: h = 0.779 and e <= 0.0039 at pi = 0.03, recall 0.90; e <= 0.0077 at recall 0.80 (baseline LightGBM)
limitations: pi is an upper bound (<3%), so e is an upper bound; recall 'over 90%' is the graph-feature model, 'close to 80%' the baseline
